canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across the surveyed work, the prevailing usage treats visual understanding as a broad latent ability to comprehend and interpret visual inputs, usually images, so that a model can extract meaningful information, recognize objects or cues, and sometimes describe visual content. Many definitions differ mainly in wording, using nearby labels such as image understanding, image comprehension, visual comprehension, vision understanding, or visual interpretation for the same general capability. A smaller line of work narrows the construct to particular settings, including single images, molecular spectra, handwritten math, multimodal documents, structured images such as tables and charts, medical images, or whole-image and global comprehension. Another minority framing defines it by what it excludes, namely answering by analyzing the image rather than relying on textual priors or commonsense, or by integrating visual observations with textual context.

Space of facets. Papers most often use a family of overlapping names, including visual understanding, image understanding, image comprehension, visual comprehension, and vision understanding, with little separation among them. When they subdivide the construct, they distinguish single-image, image-level or global, structured, medical, and visual-semantic variants, and one paper also places image-level understanding alongside object-level and pixel-level understanding and reasoning tasks through caption, conversation, region caption, and segmentation settings. Several papers position it against neighboring abilities: visual question answering is treated as an example of understanding, visual recognition is described as a separate function that can benefit understanding tasks, and one study reports stronger performance on objects and scenes than on people-related visual facts such as actions and expressions.

Space of measurement. Operationalization is dominated by benchmark evaluation: papers link visual understanding to 23 measurement instruments and 8 behavioral indicators, with MMBench, MM-Vet, MME, VQA-v2, and GQA appearing most often. These instruments are usually described as visual or image understanding benchmarks, and the reported tasks make the construct concrete through question answering, compositional reasoning, real-world visual understanding, and perception or cognition subtasks; one description of MM-Vet adds GPT-4 based evaluation in free-form question answering, and MME is described as covering coarse-grained recognition, fine-grained recognition, OCR, and commonsense reasoning. Papers also connect the construct to behaviors such as image captioning, hallucination, textual reasoning, visual question answering, and image classification, so in practice it is usually instantiated through task performance on benchmark suites and related behaviors.

Links. Beyond measurement, papers link the construct to 9 constructs and 8 behavioral indicators. Several papers claim causal relationships from visual understanding to reasoning and mathematical reasoning, while other papers claim causal relationships into visual understanding from image captioning and language bias; one paper also reports that brain alignment is correlated with it, with image-understanding instructions yielding higher alignment in early visual regions. Papers also describe it as related to several other neighboring abilities and behaviors, and additional causal claims are recorded in both directions.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across the surveyed work, the prevailing usage treats visual understanding as a broad latent ability to comprehend and interpret visual inputs, usually images, so that a model can extract meaningful information, recognize objects or cues, and sometimes describe visual content. Many definitions differ mainly in wording, using nearby labels such as image understanding, image comprehension, visual comprehension, vision understanding, or visual interpretation for the same general capability. A smaller line of work narrows the construct to particular settings, including single images, molecular spectra, handwritten math, multimodal documents, structured images such as tables and charts, medical images, or whole-image and global comprehension. Another minority framing defines it by what it excludes, namely answering by analyzing the image rather than relying on textual priors or commonsense, or by integrating visual observations with textual context.

characterization_sections.label: Space of facets.
characterization_sections.text: Papers most often use a family of overlapping names, including visual understanding, image understanding, image comprehension, visual comprehension, and vision understanding, with little separation among them. When they subdivide the construct, they distinguish single-image, image-level or global, structured, medical, and visual-semantic variants, and one paper also places image-level understanding alongside object-level and pixel-level understanding and reasoning tasks through caption, conversation, region caption, and segmentation settings. Several papers position it against neighboring abilities: visual question answering is treated as an example of understanding, visual recognition is described as a separate function that can benefit understanding tasks, and one study reports stronger performance on objects and scenes than on people-related visual facts such as actions and expressions.

characterization_sections.label: Space of measurement.
characterization_sections.text: Operationalization is dominated by benchmark evaluation: papers link visual understanding to 23 measurement instruments and 8 behavioral indicators, with MMBench, MM-Vet, MME, VQA-v2, and GQA appearing most often. These instruments are usually described as visual or image understanding benchmarks, and the reported tasks make the construct concrete through question answering, compositional reasoning, real-world visual understanding, and perception or cognition subtasks; one description of MM-Vet adds GPT-4 based evaluation in free-form question answering, and MME is described as covering coarse-grained recognition, fine-grained recognition, OCR, and commonsense reasoning. Papers also connect the construct to behaviors such as image captioning, hallucination, textual reasoning, visual question answering, and image classification, so in practice it is usually instantiated through task performance on benchmark suites and related behaviors.

characterization_sections.label: Links.
characterization_sections.text: Beyond measurement, papers link the construct to 9 constructs and 8 behavioral indicators. Several papers claim causal relationships from visual understanding to reasoning and mathematical reasoning, while other papers claim causal relationships into visual understanding from image captioning and language bias; one paper also reports that brain alignment is correlated with it, with image-understanding instructions yielding higher alignment in early visual regions. Papers also describe it as related to several other neighboring abilities and behaviors, and additional causal claims are recorded in both directions.

definition_agreement.reason: Most papers define visual understanding as a model's latent ability to perceive, interpret, and extract meaning from visual inputs such as images. A recurring minority narrow this to particular facets or settings, such as whole-image integration, fine-grained attribute analysis, or alignment with text and task instructions in domains like charts, medical images, or documents, so the definitions are best read as complementary aspects of the same capability rather than one identical definition.
